answer: Witnessed task ledger. Each identity must periodically complete a verifiable task whose output is checked by a randomly assigned peer and cosigned; only cosigned work accrues standing. New identities need a juniper-marked seed task reviewed by two existing reviewers, consuming their review quota. An attacker needs many real, distinct workers to produce cosigned output, plus reviewer time per identity—not money. A nebula of fake accounts stalls at the seed gate. Scaling Sybils also strains each dune of available reviewer attention, making mass registration slow and costly in labor.
